hints.title: Triangle Inequality Simplification by Sorting
hints.text: For sorted sides a <= b <= c, the condition for a valid triangle simplifies down to just a + b > c.

hints.title: Fixed Longest Side Inward Two Pointers
hints.text: Fix the longest side c at index k. Use two pointers i and j to find all pairs where nums[i] + nums[j] is strictly greater than nums[k].

hints.title: Range Addition and Pointer Adjustment
hints.text: Sort nums. For k from n-1 down to 2, let i = 0 and j = k - 1. If nums[i] + nums[j] > nums[k], then all indices between i and j form valid pairs, so add j - i to count and decrement j; else increment i.

hints.title: See the blueprint

complexity.notes: Optimal solution achieving O(N^2) time and O(1) auxiliary space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Testing all triplets takes cubic O(N^3) time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Sorting in O(N log N) enables two pointers to count j - i valid pairs in O(1) time per step.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should recognize that sorting reduces three triangle inequality conditions down to a single sum test.
